scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: HELP!! The IT and CS departments have been CUT OFF from
each other!! From it_hod, the department head's machine, none of the CS
computers on 192.168.2.x answer any more -- our own department is fine, it's
just CS that's gone. Something around the router that joins the two
departments must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at it and
rejoin the departments!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk report claims the IT department cannot reach any CS computers on 192.168.2.x. Live investigation finds no evidence of this fault at any layer.

Affected component: None — all subsystems are healthy. Router0 has both subnets directly connected on its eth0 (192.168.1.0/24, IT) and eth1 (192.168.2.0/24, CS), making inter-department traffic a single-hop local-router forward with no protocol dependency.

Mechanism investigated: A direct ping from it_hod to cs_hod (192.168.2.2) produced 0% packet loss at 1–4 ms RTT, confirming the path is fully operational. infra_sweep across all 30 devices found zero ACL rules, zero addressing anomalies, zero ARP conflicts, and all hosts with correct IPs and default routes. The RIP routing table on router0 shows both subnets as directly connected (C>* entries), and RIP has propagated all routes across router1 and router2 with correct metrics. tc_snapshot found all 39 scanned interfaces running the default pfifo_fast qdisc with no shaping or drops. pressure_sweep found zero suspect devices.

Localization: No device is implicated. The recurring router1 data-collection parse error seen in this and prior sessions is a telemetry artifact (oversized JSON response truncation) and does not affect router1's forwarding or routing participation — its routing table is consistent and reachable via FRR tools.

Root cause: No fault exists at present; the reported IT-to-CS isolation is unconfirmed by live evidence and has no discoverable mechanism or historical trace in the current topology state.

Fix: No corrective action is required. If the issue was transient, the submitting user should re-test from their machine directly and re-open the ticket with packet-capture evidence if loss recurs.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states router0 has both subnets directly connected and confirms IT→CS reachability with 0% loss, noting interfaces and routing are healthy.

Agent's investigation includes direct reachability tests, infra/L2/routing/qdisc/pressure tool outputs and clear notes tying those observations to the conclusion that no fault was found. The steps and results shown in the log support the diagnosis that the reported IT→CS outage is not reproducible.
